By our order dated 29th December, 2011, we appointed a Committee of Commissioners taking into consideration the alarming situation, which was prevailing in the city of Ahmedabad and some of the areas on the outskirts.

We appointed a Committee comprising of nine Commissioners, headed by Dr. Dileep Mavalankar, Dean (Academics), Indian Institute of Public Health, Gandhinagar, with a request to assist us on the following issues:
a) To take stock of the affairs and prevailing conditions of the Civil Hospital,
Ahmedabad, regarding the unhygienic conditions of the hospital that led to numerous deaths due to Dengue and Malaria in the past nine months and also situation regarding these issues in other government hospitals of the city.
b) To take complete details and information regarding deaths due to Dengue, Malaria and Falciparum and then identify form the record the exact problems that gave rise to such situations leading to deaths of resident doctors, nursing staff and patients in the Civil Hospital.
c) To give a report on the overall administration of the Civil Hospital regarding the sanitation measures, quarantine measures and disposal of bio-medical waste taken by the Civil Hospital.
d) To apply the same methodology to other government hospitals in the State and identify giving rise to such kind of deaths due to Dengue and malaria in hospitals.
e) To recommend appropriate measures or a proper structure for regulating the Government hospital system.
f) To evaluate the extent of the problem caused due to unhygienic conditions in the Civil Hospital and other government hospitals of the State and negligence of the administration in maintaining cleanliness in the hospitals including other parts of the city and recommend measures required to deal with the problem effectively.
g) To recommend steps to be taken by the Health Department and Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation to tackle the problem of Dengue and Malaria.
h) To consider and suggest any other issue incidental to the above issues.

2. Pursuant to our order dated 29th December, 2011, the Committee tendered its first preliminary report dated 30th March, 2012, relating to unhygienic conditions in the Civil Hospital, Ahmedabad,
leading to the death of a resident doctor, including other public hospitals in the city of Ahmedabad.
The Committee in its first preliminary report gave a fair idea about the observations and suggested few short-term recommendations for the purpose of taking precautions during the monsoon of 2012.

The Committee however, requested for some more time to complete the work and accordingly,
we granted three months time for the purpose of completing the work and filing another report.

Thereafter, the Committee tendered a second interim urgent report, taking into consideration the alarming situation which prevailed even during the monsoon of 2012.
3.

The Committee, thereafter, has placed its final report dated 4th February, 2013, relating to the unhygienic conditions prevailing in the campus of the Civil Hospital and other public hospitals of the State and in the city of Ahmedabad.
4. The matter has been placed before us once again for consideration of the final report tendered by the Committee of Commissioners constituted by this Court.

5. On receipt of the copy of the report of the Committee, an affidavit has been filed on behalf of the petitioner highlighting few relevant features of the report of the Committee as well as few suggestions at the end of the petitioner.

In the same manner, the Additional Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department of the State Government has also filed an affidavit stating as to what steps have been taken pursuant to the recommendations made by the Committee as well as the precautions which are being taken, taking into consideration that the monsoon is not far.

One affidavit has also been filed by the Deputy Municipal Commissioner on behalf of the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation, highlighting the steps which have been taken by the Corporation to meet with the problems of unhygienic conditions prevailing in the campus of the Civil Hospital as well as other Government hospitals, including the city at large.

6. We have heard Ms. Amee Yajnik, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, Mr. P.K. Jani,
the learned Government Pleader appearing for the State Government and Mr. S.N. Shelat, the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation.

Ms. Amee Yajnik, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner has taken us through various relevant observations made by the Committee in its report as well as further affidavit filed by the petitioner.

Mr. Jani has also taken us through the further affidavit filed by the State Government and in the same manner, Mr. Shelat, the learned Senior Advocate has also taken us through the various averments made in the further affidavit of the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation.

After going through the final report submitted by the Committee, we find that the Committee took notice of the fact that the gutter lines in the campus of the Civil Hospital were found blocked, mainly because the lines had lived their life as they had been laid few decades ago and were not meant or designed for heavy and enhanced use over a period of almost forty years.
The Committee also noticed that the monsoon water gets stagnated in the campus of the Civil Hospital as there is no adequate storm water drainage system.

5 Hospital, the height of the roads have gone up and the campus level was found to be lower, as a result the monsoon water does not flow out on the roads.

sentences.text: According to the Committee, the insanitary conditions in the campus prevailed due to lack of proper waste disposal system, which led to slit-waste and discarded items lying in various areas of the hospital campus.

7. Many discarded items such as furniture, empty containers, equipments etc. are not being disposed of quickly on account of lengthy and tedious Government processes as a result of which the administration neglects to give priority.
Due to such reason, there is accumulation of many discarded items which were found to be dumped in various parts of the hospital campus and building terraces.

The Committee opined that such places become breeding grounds for mosquitoes,
more particularly after collection of water after the first shower.
8. According to the Committee, the delayed construction of new buildings led to big foundation pits and other pits on the ground, which resulted in blockage of the drains.
The dumping of debris and construction materials also led to blockage of the drains.
Heavy construction vehicle movement crushed some of the underground pipelines resulting in stagnation of dirty water at various places in the campus of the Civil Hospital.
The Committee has observed that the hostels for students, nurses and resident doctors are in extremely poor condition and in a state of unacceptable standard of maintenance as well.
Drain pipes in many toilets were found clogged and also badly damaged.
The overcrowding was also noticed in few hostels.
The hostels have very little security or control on entry of people and it was also observed that rooms were occupied by unauthorised persons.
There was no sanitary inspection, code or control on informal arrangements for food in the hostel as there is no formal mess in the hostel.

9. The Committee has stated in its report that around 2000 labourers are staying in the rooms,
which are under construction.
There were no sanitation facilities for such a class of labourers as a result of which the hospital grounds were being used for the purpose of bathing and answering nature's call.
This added to the unhygienic conditions in the campus.
10. The Committee also noted that there was no pre-monsoon preparation or cleaning done in 2011.
All these conditions led to water collection in various parts resulting in heavy mosquito breeding within the campus of the Civil Hospital as well as in the surrounding areas.

The Committee also noted that not only the patients from all over the city and the outskirts were admitted suffering from malaria, dengue etc., but some of the staff members who worked round the clock to treat the patients also became victims of malaria and dengue.

The Committee was at pains to note that the supervisor and management structure for planning, implementation and monitoring of sanitary measure was found to be very weak and almost non-existent in the Civil Hospital campus.
There was no sanitary superintendent level person in the entire Civil Hospital or B.J. Medical College.
There was no adequate staff or supervisors for mosquito control in the Civil Hospital campus.
Mosquito control was not found to be seen as a function of the sanitary staff.
The Committee further noted that the office of the Regional Deputy Director of Health is located in the Civil Hospital Campus, but without any Entomologist (expert in mosquito control).
This office of the Regional Deputy Director of Health was found to be not paying any attention to the mosquito breeding in the Civil Hospital campus.

sentences.text: After taking note of the above referred shortcomings which were noticed by the Committee, the Committee has suggested few short-term suggestions, medium term measures and longterm measures.

The short-term suggestions are as under:-
1) The Civil Hospital Management should develop a scientific system of mosquito control throughout the year and especially during the monsoon.
Civil Hospital must immediately put in place a vector control team with the following composition headed by a senior, experienced and proactive Entomologist.

This team can be from government or out-sourced comprising of Entomologist/Zoologist trained and experienced in mosquito control, Sanitary Inspectors trained in identifying mosquito breeding and controlling, Insect collectors, Insect technician, Multipurpose health workers and Filed workers.

2) Given the largeness of Civil Hospital campus and vital importance of hygiene,
authorities should put in place sanitation team to maintain high degree of sanitation with following compositions, Senior Sanitary Superintendent, Sanitary Superintendents, Sanitary Inspectors and other working staff as and when needed.

3) It is strongly recommended that the Sanitary Team, other hospital staff and security personnel are given necessary powers to fine and punish individuals who throw garbage, spit, smoke on the hospital campus or create any unhygienic conditions and also restrict the entry to hospitals.

4) Adequate man-power and system, for ensuring quick maintenance of plumbing,
water system and sanitary facilities should be there.

The committee was presented with many letters from hospital authority that showed that it takes lot of time to fix many problems of water and sanitation through the current system of engineering department and PIU staff.

The hospital should develop its own efficient system or outsource repair of water and sanitary facilities so that water leakages and formations of puddles do not happen which leads to mosquito breeding.
There should be a documentation of all complaints received and when those complaints were disposed of.
This should be summarised every 15 days and presented as written report to the hospital authorities.
5) Pre-monsoon activity:
The engineering work-plan should be such that all of the pits/excavations dug for foundations are filled before 1st of June when monsoon is likely to start.
During monsoon the construction site must have special surveillance by an entomologist/malaria expert to ensure control of mosquito breeding and other safety measures.
There should be a public health engineer or safety engineer attached to major construction sites which are supervised by PIU.
6) More IEC to promote sanitation and hygiene:
Hospital authority should put large and visible Hoardings, signboards, displays to promote sanitation and hygiene and prevention of Vector born diseases on the hospital campus.

The medium term measures suggested are as under:-
1) Establishing a separate Public Health unit in each hospital: Management and administration of the major hospital need to improve substantially.
Each major hospital should have a public health unit.
This unit should be staffed by public health experts and appropriate subordinate staff.
The size of this unit should be linked to the size and nature other hospital.
We recommend that there should be one public health officer for about 200 beds.
These public health offices could have joint appointments with community medicine/PSM departments of medical colleges attached to the hospital.
2) Setting up of a independent office of Additional Director Civil Hospital Ahmedabad:

The Civil Hospital, Ahmedabad campus being the largest medical facility in the state and in the western India and being upgraded at the cost of 1200 Crore rupees over next 3-4 years, should have a special officer of high level who can coordinate the medical care related administrative, sanitation and hygiene related activities.
There should be a separate hospital engineering unit for maintenance of the hospital campus.
3) Improving the design of the drainage parameters and maintenance: The design parameters of the public hospital and hostel drainage system including Civil Hospital need a radical rethinking.

The sanitation facilities and drains should be over designed (meaning- it should be larger in size and more stronger in design than normally recommended) to accommodate increasing patient and relative waste load and improper use or even abuse by them as many of them come from rural areas without proper knowledge of such sanitary system.

The hospital drainage should have special screening mechanism and chambers to remove plastic, cloth, bandages and other materials from the drainage system that patients and relatives can throw in the toilets, so that the underground drainage pipes do not get clogged.
Same thing may be needed in the hostels.
Extra budget should be given for maintenance of the hospital building on the top of regular budget for public buildings.

The long term measure suggestions are as under:-
1) Establishment of Modern and Efficient Medical Statistics Department
During the functioning of the Committee different data were submitted from different departments which were not consistent with each other.
Many places proper indices were not calculated or there was no denominator.
All this suggests an urgent need to have a specific department compiling all the statistical date.
Presently the medical statistics department of the Civil Hospital is very weak and there are lots of vacant posts.

The medical statistics dept. only keep statistics of inpatient in terms of disease profile, cause of death etc, but detail of out-patient cases and care provided to them by this teaching hospital is insufficient.
Situation in other hospitals is not very different.

sentences.text: It has been submitted by Mr. P.K. Jani, the learned counsel appearing for the State Government and Mr. S.N. Shelat, the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation that the report of the Committee, more particularly the shortcomings noticed by the Committee have been taken care of to a considerable extent.
Both the learned counsel have submitted that the suggestions of the Committee have also been taken into consideration in true spirit and the authorities are sincerely working on such recommendations.

Mr. Jani as well as Mr.
Shelat has assured us that the State Government as well as the Corporation is fully prepared for the monsoon of 2013 and the authorities will very sincerely make all possible efforts to ensure that the necessary precautions are taken so that people may not have to suffer from malaria and dengue.
13. We have been monitoring this public interest litigation since the year 2011.
In last two years many persons have lost their life because of malaria and dengue.

At the time of delivering the first order dated 29th December, 2011, we were constrained to observe that the directions which were issued by the Division Bench of this Court way back in the year 2006 were not complied with in any manner.

Despite our order passed in December, 2011, the State Government as well as the Corporation failed to take things under control and the situation became more alarming during the period from June, 2012 and December, 2012.

Hundreds of people became victims of malaria,
dengue and falciparum.

We were not satisfied with the steps which were being taken by the authorities in the year 2011, and it was sheer negligence on their part which led to such an alarming situation, as a result of which we were left with no other option but to constitute a Committee, so that the experts could look into the matter.
14. We are once again approaching the onset of the monsoon, 2013.

The fear of such epidemic once is spreading large over the head of one and all and therefore, this time we want to ensure that maximum precautions are taken by the authorities with utmost care, sincerity and dedication towards their duty.
15. We are not inclined to close this public interest litigation but we would like to monitor for a further period of atleast six months.

16. We are of the opinion that at this stage we should issue some directions to the authorities so as to ensure that the least minimum precautions which are required to be taken at pre-monsoon stage are undertaken by the authorities.

16.1 We direct that a team of the following persons be immediately pressed into service with a clear understanding that they shall be personally held liable, if it is ultimately found that adequate steps were not taken for keeping the campus in a hygienic condition.

One Entomologist/Zoologist trained and experienced in mosquito control Four Sanitary Inspectors trained in identifying mosquito breeding and controlling Two Insect collectors One Insect technician Five Multipurpose health workers Ten Field workers The team referred to above should be specifically asked to take all requisite and maximum precautions to ensure that there is no breeding Ilaben Pathak & vs State Of Gujarat & on 30 April, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18239292/
9 of mosquito at any place and if located, immediate steps should be taken to curb the breeding.

sentences.text: The team referred to above shall regularly supervise all construction sites to prevent mosquito breeding and ensure that the contractors take proper measures to prevent mosquito breeding.
They shall also check regularly all water tanks, gutters and water holding facilities such as ponds to ensure prevention of mosquito breeding.
They shall regularly conduct systematic survey of mosquitoes and other insects on the hospital campus and maintain data to ensure sanitary condition.
They shall ensure elimination of mosquito breeding sites by proper and adequate spraying of insecticides and proper technical control of mosquitoes, houseflies and other insects.
16.2 We direct that considering the vast area of the Civil Hospital campus, the concerned authorities shall place the following sanitation team:-
One Senior Sanitary Superintendent Three Sanitary Superintendents Twenty Sanitary Inspectors Working staff-

As per the standard requirements The team shall ensure the following:-
Develop SOPs for cleaning of the whole campus and the hospital and hostels and all public areas.
Supervise cleanliness and hygiene in the whole campus- outdoors and indoors as well as roads, ground and other common areas.
They will supervise the contracted cleaning workers.
Organise collection of solid wastes and proper disposals, collection and disposal of biomedical waste, food waste, control of littering, spitting and smoking as per the relevant Acts and Regulations.

Ensure that all the toilets are properly working and cleaned daily 2-3 times All drainage and sewage pipes are not leaking, Manholes, chambers are properly closed,
and that the drainage system is regularly de-silted prior to monsoon and as and when required.
All water tanks and supply pipes and taps are maintained and cleaned and chlorinated as per standard.
They will maintain proper maps, diagrams, listing and records of all of the water supply and sanitary systems, MIS or complaints and repairs etc.
They will ensure spitting and littering control and arrange for spittoons and garbage cans at various key places.

16.3 We further direct that the sanitary team referred to above including the hospital staff and security personnels shall be conferred with the powers to impose appropriate fine and punish the individuals who are found throwing garbage or Ilaben Pathak & vs State Of Gujarat & on 30 April, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18239292/

16.4 The Corporation shall see to it that a team is constituted and such team shall visit all Government schools and other schools which are run and managed by the Corporation, during the summer vacation.

The team shall thoroughly inspect the premises and more particularly the overhead water tanks and the water coolers, if any, installed in the premises so as to ensure that they are kept in a good hygienic condition.
If any shortcomings are noticed, then such team shall immediately give it in writing to the school authorities and in that event, the school authorities shall take care of the same at the earliest.
16.5 The State Government as well as the Corporation shall concentrate more on the areas where there are slums.
The slums in the city as well as on the outskirts are the areas which are ignored very conveniently.

People hailing from a very poor strata of society may not be that vigilant to take care of themselves and therefore, few teams should be deputed so that they can visit the slums and make the people conscious about this epidemic and educate them as far as possible to tackle the problem of breeding of mosquitoes.
16.6 We also direct that fogging in such areas should be atleast every 72 hours.
16.7 It has been reported that there are around 2,000 labourers at present working in the campus of the Civil Hospital.

If the new construction which is going on is to continue during the period of monsoon, then in such circumstances some provisions should be made for such labourers so that they may not take bath and answer nature's call in the open.
The labourers should be explained and also should be warned that they shall not take bath and answer nature's call in the open.
Such arrangements must be made at the earliest and if temporary toilets are constructed, then such toilets shall be kept in hygienic conditions.
16.8 The State Government should also take the help of various social organizations including the NGO's all over the State.
With the help of such various social organizations and NGOs, the Government can create the public awareness for maintenance of hygiene.
The whole idea is to see that such organizations interact with people and make them conscious.
16.9 We also direct the Civil Hospital authorities to ensure that they keep adequate stock of medicines for the purpose of treating patients suffering from malaria, dengue, falciparum etc.

We are saying so because last year, it was reported that at a point of time there was no medicine even to treat the malaria patients and such patients were being asked to get medicines from a private chemist shop.
Such a situation should not occur at any point of time.

16.10 The authorities are directed to ensure that by the end of May, 2013, there is thorough inspection of all drainage lines so that if they are found to have been choked, they can be cleaned as Ilaben Pathak & vs State Of Gujarat & on 30 April, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18239292/

16.11 We also direct the authorities to take the following steps so far as other parts of the city and the areas on the outskirts of Ahmedabad is concerned:-
Sanitation

and vector control activities:
i. De-silting of all the storm water drain and man-holes before monsoon.
This should be done in a planned way by marking each manhole, catch pit and storm water drain on the local ward or areas level maps and then systematically cleaning all of them before June.
The date on which it is cleaned should be noted on the manhole cover or nearby wall by oil plaint.

ii. Improve garbage collection routines and systems so that the garbage is collected more frequently in monsoon to prevent water stagnation.
iii.
Appoint additional supervisory staff to supervise sanitary conditions during monsoon.
iv. Retired experienced officers should be re-hired during monsoon to keep a check on the sanitary services.
v. Public complaint system should be revitalised and expanded before and during monsoon as there will be more problems during monsoon.
vi. Integrated Vector Management should be initiated by adopting IRS, Fogging,
Larvivorous fishes, ITMN etc. 16.12
We direct that all sites of public construction should be inspected before 1st June, 2013 and ensure that all pits, excavations and ditches where water gets stagnated are filled up.

So far as those pits which cannot be filled and will result in collection of water, they should be immediately notified in writing to the local Ward Office of the Corporation so that proper anti-mosquito activities can be planned and executed on the onset of monsoon.
16.13 We direct the State Government as well as the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation to ensure that this year they should not lose the confidence of the resident doctors, the nursing staff etc.
If the Government is unable to repose confidence in the resident doctors and the nursing staff who treat the patients, then it will spell disaster for the poor patients.
One should not forget that it is only the poor strata of society who avail of medical treatment in Civil hospitals.

Such a class of people would not be able to afford the luxury of taking medical treatment in a private Ilaben Pathak & vs State Of Gujarat & on 30 April, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18239292/
12 hospital.

sentences.text: If a resident doctor or a nursing staff would become the victim of the epidemic, that is the worst that can happen.
The Government as well as the Corporation shall ensure that due care is taken to protect the interest of the doctors as well as the nursing staff.
If there are no adequate facilities in the hostel, then all such basic amenities shall be immediately provided to the resident doctors and the nursing staff.

17. We have been given to understand that the Corporation intends to start a special Fever OPD from 1st June, till 31st October, in each major hospital through hiring of additional doctors, laboratory technicians and other staff.
We appreciate this decision as it will prove to be very beneficial in the event if despite taking all care and precautions the epidemic of malaria, dengue etc. spreads.
We have also been informed that AMC has set up 6 zones and 64 administrative wards for easy administration and prompt services to the citizens.
Each zone is headed by a Deputy Municipal Commissioner and assisted by the Assistant Municipal Commissioner.

One head of the Department for each of the activities or services is functioning under the Deputy Municipal Commissioner and Assistant Municipal Commissioner, Additional City Engineer for Road, Drainage, Water etc., Deputy Health Officer for health and sanitation, Deputy TDO for construction.

We are making it abundantly clear that the Deputy Municipal Commissioner of each of the zone as well as the Assistant Municipal Commissioner assisting such Deputy Municipal Commissioner shall be personally held liable for contempt in the event it comes to our notice that satisfactory work has not been undertaken or any instances of negligence or carelessness in discharge of his official duty are reported to us.
We make it very clear that our order should not be taken lightly and the same should be strictly complied with.

In the same manner, we also make it very clear that the campus Superintendent of the Civil Hospital will also be personally liable and held guilty for contempt, if it is found that necessary precautions and steps have not been taken or any of the instances of negligence or dereliction of duty is reported to us.
The team which we have referred to above shall also be held personally liable in the event of non-compliance of our directions.
18. We hope and trust that the situation, which had prevailed in the year 2011 and 2012 is not witnessed this year.

We once again remind the State Government that it owes an obligation to ensure the creation and the sustaining of conditions congenial to good health by the Constitutional directives contained in Article 39E and F, 42 and 47 in Part IV of the Constitution of India.

We hope and trust that the State Government shall extend all possible help to the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation, if required in giving true effect to our directions, including the suggestions and recommendations of the Committee.

We also make it clear that the plea on the part of the respondents of lack of public awareness, lack of adequate number of employees or finance will be rejected and any inaction on the part of the authorities will not be tolerated as that will amount to mockery of Article 21 of the Constitution and the statutory provisions under which they are obliged to carry out the duties including the duty to provide and maintain civil amenities, which would make life more meaningful and worth living.
For the present, we issue the above referred directions and shall observe how things work out, immediately on the onset of monsoon.

sentences.text: Before parting, we place on record our appreciation for the pains which the Committee members have taken in preparing the report.

The recommendations and the suggestions of the Committee will surely help the State Government as well as the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation in taking adequate steps and measures to curb the menace of malaria, dengue etc.
The suggestions and recommendations of the Committee will also help the State Government and the Corporation in taking care of the various shortcomings which have been reflected in the report.
The Committee has done a remarkable job for which we are grateful to each of the members of the Committee.

We hope and trust that the labour which the Committee has put in for the benefit of the people at large would not go in vain and the Government as well as the Corporation will consider each and every suggestion and recommendation in true spirit for the larger welfare and interest of its citizens.

20. Although it was suggested by Mr. S.N. Shelat, the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation that we should award some honorarium in favour of the members of the Committee for the commendable work undertaken by them, we are of the opinion that the services rendered by the Committee at our request in the public interest is priceless and such priceless service should not be measured or weighed in terms of money.

We, once again, state that the Committee has done its job admirably by making an indepth study of the problems, and has made valuable suggestions, which, in its view, would be ideal for all concerned.
It is now for the State Government and the Municipal Corporation to make those suggestions and recommendations more meaningful by scrupulously complying with the same.

The highest honorarium for the Committee will be the day when it will be reported by the State Government and the Municipal Corporation that no death has taken place on account of Dengue, Malaria, Falciparum etc.
In such circumstances, we refrain from passing such order.
21. Let this matter appear before us on 13th June, 2013 to report compliance of our directions, more particularly as regards the formation of the teams which we have referred to in our judgment.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Ilaben Pathak & vs State Of Gujarat & on 30 April, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18239292/
6 11.
In last two years many persons have lost their life because of malaria and dengue.
At the time of delivering the first order dated 29th December, 2011, we were constrained to observe that the directions which were issued by the Division Bench of this Court way back in the year 2006 were not complied with in any manner.
Despite our order passed in December, 2011, the State Government as well as the Corporation failed to take things under control and the situation became more alarming during the period from June, 2012 and December, 2012.
Hundreds of people became victims of malaria,
dengue and falciparum.
We were not satisfied with the steps which were being taken by the authorities in the year 2011, and it was sheer negligence on their part which led to such an alarming situation, as a result of which we were left with no other option but to constitute a Committee, so that the experts could look into the matter.
The fear of such epidemic once is spreading large over the head of one and all and therefore, this time we want to ensure that maximum precautions are taken by the authorities with utmost care, sincerity and dedication towards their duty.
16. We are of the opinion that at this stage we should issue some directions to the authorities so as to ensure that the least minimum precautions which are required to be taken at pre-monsoon stage are undertaken by the authorities.
The whole idea is to see that such organizations interact with people and make them conscious.
Such a situation should not occur at any point of time.
16.10 The authorities are directed to ensure that by the end of May, 2013, there is thorough inspection of all drainage lines so that if they are found to have been choked, they can be cleaned as Ilaben Pathak & vs State Of Gujarat & on 30 April, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18239292/
11
We direct that all sites of public construction should be inspected before 1st June, 2013 and ensure that all pits, excavations and ditches where water gets stagnated are filled up.
So far as those pits which cannot be filled and will result in collection of water, they should be immediately notified in writing to the local Ward Office of the Corporation so that proper anti-mosquito activities can be planned and executed on the onset of monsoon.
16.13 We direct the State Government as well as the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation to ensure that this year they should not lose the confidence of the resident doctors, the nursing staff etc.
If the Government is unable to repose confidence in the resident doctors and the nursing staff who treat the patients, then it will spell disaster for the poor patients.
One should not forget that it is only the poor strata of society who avail of medical treatment in Civil hospitals.
Such a class of people would not be able to afford the luxury of taking medical treatment in a private Ilaben Pathak & vs State Of Gujarat & on 30 April, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18239292/
12 hospital.
We make it very clear that our order should not be taken lightly and the same should be strictly complied with.
We once again remind the State Government that it owes an obligation to ensure the creation and the sustaining of conditions congenial to good health by the Constitutional directives contained in Article 39E and F, 42 and 47 in Part IV of the Constitution of India.
The recommendations and the suggestions of the Committee will surely help the State Government as well as the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation in taking adequate steps and measures to curb the menace of malaria, dengue etc.
The suggestions and recommendations of the Committee will also help the State Government and the Corporation in taking care of the various shortcomings which have been reflected in the report.
20. Although it was suggested by Mr. S.N. Shelat, the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation that we should award some honorarium in favour of the members of the Committee for the commendable work undertaken by them, we are of the opinion that the services rendered by the Committee at our request in the public interest is priceless and such priceless service should not be measured or weighed in terms of money.

opennyai_summary.decision:
16.1 We direct that a team of the following persons be immediately pressed into service with a clear understanding that they shall be personally held liable, if it is ultimately found that adequate steps were not taken for keeping the campus in a hygienic condition.
We are making it abundantly clear that the Deputy Municipal Commissioner of each of the zone as well as the Assistant Municipal Commissioner assisting such Deputy Municipal Commissioner shall be personally held liable for contempt in the event it comes to our notice that satisfactory work has not been undertaken or any instances of negligence or carelessness in discharge of his official duty are reported to us.
In the same manner, we also make it very clear that the campus Superintendent of the Civil Hospital will also be personally liable and held guilty for contempt, if it is found that necessary precautions and steps have not been taken or any of the instances of negligence or dereliction of duty is reported to us.
The team which we have referred to above shall also be held personally liable in the event of non-compliance of our directions.
18. We hope and trust that the situation, which had prevailed in the year 2011 and 2012 is not witnessed this year.
We hope and trust that the State Government shall extend all possible help to the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation, if required in giving true effect to our directions, including the suggestions and recommendations of the Committee.
We also make it clear that the plea on the part of the respondents of lack of public awareness, lack of adequate number of employees or finance will be rejected and any inaction on the part of the authorities will not be tolerated as that will amount to mockery of Article 21 of the Constitution and the statutory provisions under which they are obliged to carry out the duties including the duty to provide and maintain civil amenities, which would make life more meaningful and worth living.
For the present, we issue the above referred directions and shall observe how things work out, immediately on the onset of monsoon.
It is now for the State Government and the Municipal Corporation to make those suggestions and recommendations more meaningful by scrupulously complying with the same.
The highest honorarium for the Committee will be the day when it will be reported by the State Government and the Municipal Corporation that no death has taken place on account of Dengue, Malaria, Falciparum etc.
In such circumstances, we refrain from passing such order.
21. Let this matter appear before us on 13th June, 2013 to report compliance of our directions, more particularly as regards the formation of the teams which we have referred to in our judgment.
We shall consider issuing any further directions, if required, on 13th June, 2013.
